item.title: Policy Assistant, Political 4 - UN Horizontal issues Section
item.description: The European Union Delegation to the United Nations New York is looking for an: Policy Assistant in the Political 4 -UN Horizontal Issues Section (UNGA, ECOSOC, administration, financial and budgetary issues) The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. As a UN observer with enhanced status, the EU Delegation to the United Nations in New York works in close coordination with the 27 EU Member States so as to speak with one voice. The EU also works closely with the UN secretariat and its Agencies, funds & programs, partnering on a range of global issues and challenges. We offer: We are looking for an enthusiastic and service-minded candidate to fill the post of Policy Assistant, Political Section 4 – UN Horizontal issues, a Local Agent Group II. It is a 2-year contract, with the possibility of two renewals, leading to a maximum employment term of 7 years under successive fixed-term contracts. There is a possibility of an Indefinite contract upon completing the seven-year term, under reserve of budgetary availability and operational considerations. For internal candidates holding an indefinite-term contract, alternative contractual arrangements may apply in accordance with institutional policies. The team consists of -3 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed to functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will serve under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of UN Horizontal Issues Section, providing support, expertise and assistance in the substantive work on UN accountability: the oversight mechanisms (internal: the Office of Internal Oversight Services (OIOS), and external: the UN Joint Inspection Unit (JIU)), as well as the internal appeal system for misbehavior and system wide strategies for the internal organization and accountability of the UN Following main tasks and duties are currently required: Assist the Head of Section in the coordination of experts from EU Member States in intergovernmental negotiations on items on the agenda of the UN General Assembly Fifth Committee, primarily on accountability-related issues, while providing support on other agenda items as required. 1. System of Administration of Justice (AoJ) at the UN. 2. Joint inspection unit (JIU) reviews and annual programme of work. 3. Office of Internal oversight services (OIOS). 4. Administration of internal justice. 5. Activities of the Ethics Office. Represent the EU on behalf of the Head of Section when necessary. Draft policy language for negotiations and support consultations within the EU27 and with the group of like-minded countries when applicable, as well as negotiations in the General Assembly. Contribute to the drafting of reports, analyses and political assessments for the EU headquarters on UN developments, negotiations and meetings on the topics under responsibility, and on other horizontal matters (e.g. coverage of UNGA General Debate). In addition, the local agent would perform a number of coordination tasks in close consultation with the Press, Information and Coordination section: Assist with the preparation of policy and strategy papers, as well as analytical materials on horizontal issues and mappings on various political issues and processes, including for the EU Deputy Permanent Representatives’ consideration. Provide support for the preparations for the UNGA Ministerial/High-Level Week: cover UN consultations and preparations, draft speaking points, reports and correspondence. Provide a planning overview of the UNGA High-Level Week high-level events, in collaboration with the EU headquarters and the EU Member States. Create and maintain comprehensive overviews and statistics on the alignment of EU candidate countries to EU statements at the UN and their voting patterns. Assist with the coordination and consolidation of input for the Annual Management Plan (AMP) of the EU Delegation, as well as for the annual Delegation’s record of achievements under the Lisbon Treaty Obligations (statistical table), and for other reporting requests from EU headquarters that require cross-sectional input and internal coordination. Contribute to other cross-sectional briefs and speaking points for the Head of Delegation and Deputy Head of Delegation for bilateral meetings (e.g. courtesy calls) and UN discussions. This job function may be slightly modified in accordance with the needs of the Delegation. We offer a collegial atmosphere in an international environment and work in close coordination with the Administration team in supporting colleagues across the EU Delegation. The office is located at 666 Third Avenue, New York, NY 10017. Salary level ranges is dependent on relevant and verified employment experience, starting from $89K (2 years of experience), $93K (6 years of experience), $97K (10 years’ experience) etc. There is a competitive benefits package including personal leave days and public holidays, flexible working hours, health and dental insurance and a retirement savings plan. Working hours are 37.5 hours per week. The expected start date will be October 1st, 2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) Bachelor’s degree required, master’s degree is an asset Minimum of 2 years of experience in public administration and/or international relations. The professional experience must be acquired after the date on which the qualification allowing access to the post was obtained. Thorough working knowledge of written and spoken English It is important to note that the Delegation of the European Union to the United Nations does not sponsor visas for Local Agents. Applicants must have an existing and valid US work authorization that does not require sponsorship by the Delegation (i.e. EAD card, green card, US citizen, only G1 or G3 visas for the spouses of EU officials posted at an EU Member State Mission to the United Nations. A ssets/selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Flexibility is the key. The candidate should be willing to work flexible hours, as required Ability to work effectively both independently, with minimal supervision, and as part of a team. Strong coordination skills, including the ability to listen actively, consult effectively, and share information and ideas with colleagues and stakeholders. Capacity to communicate clearly and effectively, both orally and in writing; Ability to present complex matters in a simple way, demonstrate solid analytical skills, and produce high-quality briefing notes, reports and written analyses. Ease adapting to new technology and digital tools. Excellent interpersonal skills: with a positive, proactive and solution-oriented attitude. Ability to work effectively and remain calm under pressure. Openness to cultural diversity. Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify and define problems, gather and analyze relevant information, and develop practical and effective solutions. Excellent organization and time-management skills, with the ability to stay on top of multiple files at once. Ability to plan ahead and monitor implementation and follow-up. Data analysis skills are considered an asset. Experience with the work of the UN General Assembly Fifth Committee is considered an asset. item.title: Programme Officer - Regional Rapid Response Planner
item.description: We are The core business of the European Commission’s Service for Foreign Policy Instruments (FPI) is to put EU foreign policy into action - fast and flexibly - in a policy-driven approach. The Service deals with the regulatory and financial aspects of EU foreign policy. It acts as first responder to foreign policy needs and opportunities, focusing on conflict prevention and peace as well as on leveraging the EU’s influence in the world. The Service plays a crucial role in translating the European Commission’s political priorities into external action, in line with the EU’s Global Strategy for Foreign and Security Policy. The Service reports directly to the High Representative/Vice President. The Service works in close co-operation with the other services of the Commission and with the EEAS, both at headquarters and in EU Delegations. FPI staff around the globe are proud of the work that they are achieving and have a strong sense of purpose and motivation. They take, and value, a high level of personal responsibility. A policy-driven approach, a focus on priorities, solutions and impact, combined with a welcoming and supporting atmosphere, are part of the service’s corporate culture. In terms of values, the service promotes professionalism and teamwork, encourages commitment and promotes respect. It also seeks to embed trust and fairness while prioritizing effective communication at all levels. The Regional Team of FPI for the Middle and North Africa (MENA) operates from the EU Delegations to Jordan and Lebanon. It works with 16 EU Delegations / Offices in the region1, relevant external actors and with FPI and other services in Brussels to conceptualise, elaborate and implement activities funded through the Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI-Global Europe), notably under its rapid response mechanism (for crisis response and foreign policy needs) and its thematic pillar (for the stability & peace programme). Established in 2017, the Regional Team now consists of a staff of 15 at the EU Delegations to Jordan, Lebanon, Tunisia and Saudi Arabia. Team spirit, a strong sense of initiative and responsibility is a common feature of all team members. We propose We propose an attractive and challenging position as Programme Officer - Regional Rapid Response Planner - primarily planning and managing FPI actions in the region. We look for We look for an experienced, dynamic, reliable, well-organised person with a good team spirit and excellent planning and project management skills. She/he should be pro-active, flexible and able to organise the work independently with a strong sense of responsibility. She/he should be able to adjust to multiple tasks even under tight deadlines. A positive attitude, excellent writing and communication skills, excellent inter-personal skills, and good judgement are also essential, as well as a good knowledge of EU financial and contractual procedures. Availability for frequent travel in the MENA region is required. The candidate should have at least 3 years of experience in project management, preferably including for international crisis response contexts. An excellent knowledge of English is essential while a good knowledge of French is an advantage. Knowledge of the Middle East and North Africa region and relevant field experience in the region will be considered an asset. The candidate should have the ability to work in a team and in a multi-cultural environment and to handle issues of a sensitive political nature. Knowledge of EU policy and programmes relevant to conflict prevention, crisis response and peacebuilding would be an advantage. Security clearance: If not already acquired, the selected candidate must request it when taking up function. Before taking her/his duties, the selected candidate will have to undertake the Security trainings BASE and SAFE. The selected candidate should also complete the Hostile Environment Awareness Training (HEAT) once taking up duty. Applications Interested candidates should send their CV & a short motivation letter (max. 1 page) as follows: To: DELEGATION-JORDAN-VACANCY@eeas.europa.eu Subject: Application for vacancy FPI - Job no. 518710 - Programme Officer - Regional Rapid Response Planner Please indicate your CAST Application ID in your application and mention the job-Id in subject line. Only contract agents FG IV currently in the EU institutions, candidates from an FG IV EPSO CAST valid reserve list or candidates registered as FG IV in the EPSO online database will be considered for this position. Contact: Joris.Heeren@eeas.europa.eu Deadline for application: 27 August 2026 No applications will be accepted after the publication deadline.

item.title: VACANCY NOTICE Job no. 38238 - Secretary in the Political, Press and Information Section
item.description: The European Union Delegation to the Republic of North Macedonia is looking for a Local Agent position - Secretary in Political, Press and Information Section We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organisations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to North Macedonia is one of those 140 delegations. The Delegation of the European Union is the liaison between the national authorities and EU institutions. Since the decision taken by the European Council to recognise the country as a candidate for EU membership, the work of the Delegation of the European Union has focused increasingly on monitoring and reporting on compliance with the political and economic criteria for membership of the EU, and alignment of legislation with EU legislation as well as capacity to implement and enforce it. One of the Delegation's key tasks is to inform the authorities, institutions, media and citizens of the Republic of North Macedonia about the pre-accession process and about EU institutions and policies. It also maintains regular contacts with academic institutions, business community and representatives of the civil society. We offer We offer a position of Secretary in the Political, Press and Information Section (PPI). The jobholder will work under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the PPI section. The selected candidate will be offered a fixed-term employment contract (“local agent” type contract – Group III) for two years, with the possibility of renewal. We offer a competitive position in an international environment. Benefits, such as additional pension scheme and medical insurance are offered to employees and their families under certain conditions. Place of employment: Skopje. Working time: 37.5 working hours/week. Functions and duties The successful candidate will perform the following tasks: Office organisation & logistics Provide assistance with the management of the section by maintaining the agenda of the HoS and the section, including for holidays, missions and trainings. Ensure follow-up and respect of deadlines in the Section's activities. Maintain and update contact lists relevant to the Section's activities. Organise meetings for section members, meeting rooms. Draft minutes of meetings. Organise transport/drivers. Maintain co-ordination with the Delegation's Secretariat and other sections. General administrative support upon instructions. Secretarial tasks Oral and written correspondence with Government, Parliament, political and other domestic counterparts, embassies and international organizations in Skopje, HQ in Brussels, Delegations and Embassies in the region. Answering the telephone, filtering calls and taking messages, coordinate responses or responding to general inquiries and managing the e-mail exchange, functional mailboxes and calendar. Maintain and update documents in the section archive and folders on the shared drive. Ensure that all records are completed in ARES and transmit final documents to DMO for attachment. Open and request registration of incoming mail (including e-mails) in the system. Allocate registered mail to appropriate individuals and maintain up-to-date mailing lists. Draft, type, verify layout and check quality of documents presented for signature. Prepare and copy correspondence for transmission. Prepare notes, minutes, routine correspondence, presentations and other texts that are needed for the overall section activity. Missions Manage missions (MIPS), book accommodation and flights Follow mission budget consumption. Meetings, events, visits Assist in organisation of high level visits from Brussels (prepare draft programmes, logistics, protocol) in close coordination with Ministries, HQ and other stakeholders, sections in the EUD. Provide logistical support for organisation of meetings /committees/events (reception of guests / attendees, liaising with the Administration Section on preparation of the room, materials, refreshment etc.). Preparation of guest lists for Europe Day, manage invites/confirmations, etc. Other Translate incoming mail and other documents from Macedonian into English and vice versa (mostly invitations, short letters) Within the framework of the Staff Regulation, to carry out tasks linked to the job description as instructed by his/her superior(s). The tasks listed above are indicative and may change in accordance with the Delegation’s service needs and internal organisation. Eligibility criteria: Candidates for this local agent post should: Education Experience At least three years appropriate experience as a secretary, linked to the tasks requested. Experience in an international, multicultural environment an asset. Language Proficient command of Macedonian and English language (at C1 level). Knowledge of Albanian is an asset Technical knowledge Excellent IT skills (Microsoft Office, AI Chat GPT, etc.) Legal requirements Candidates must be Macedonian/Citizen of the Republic of North Macedonia, or hold a residence permit and/or work permit for the Republic of North Macedonia Assets: Organisational skills Strong organisational skills Ability to work independently and in a systematic way Analysis and Problem Solving: conceptualise problems, identify and implement solutions Communication skills Very good drafting skills; Capacity to communicate clearly at all levels; Good capacity to maintain communication and information flow within and outside the section. Interpersonal skills Personal qualities Skills and openness to adapt to changing environment and evolving ways of working High degree of discretion, confidentiality and responsibility Selection criteria: Effective communication both orally and in writing; Capacity to perform with accuracy and in a structured and methodical way tasks in a complex institutional environment; Ability to implement policies, procedures, guidelines, templates, etc; Experience in working in a team in multi-disciplinary environment and be a flexible team player; Strong experience working with the Microsoft office package; Excellent communication skills both in Macedonian and English; knowledge of Albanian Enjoys civil rights and permits for employment under local law; How to apply Interested candidates should send a motivation letter and CV in Europass format in English only to the following functional email address: eeasjobs-170@eeas.europa.eu Subject line should state: Name Surname Job.no. 38238 Candidates shall draft their CV following the European CV form, which is available at the following internet address: https://europa.eu/europass/en/create-europass-cv *Other forms of CV will not be accepted. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure by telephone. Please address any queries concerning this procedure via e-mail to delegation-north-macedonia-recruitments@eeas.europa.eu . Successful reception of your application will be confirmed via e-mail only. Deadline for sending applications is 20 August 2026 at 17.00h Skopje time. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted by e-mail and will be invited for written test and interview. Interviews will be held in Skopje, at the EU Delegation premises. The candidates who have not been short-listed will be informed on the decision.

item.title: EEAS Call for Expression of Interest for the recruitment of one Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) as Secretary (AST/SC2) POL.MULTILATERAL – Multilateral Relations, Human Rights and Democracy Depu
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The Directorate for Multilateral Relations, Human Rights and Democracy falls under the responsibility of the DSG for POL. The Directorate aims at strengthening cooperation with the UN, the Council of Europe and other multilateral fora. More particularly, its objective is to promote universal values and EU priorities through cohesive and effective action in multilateral fora and to protect and defend human rights and democracy as an integral part of the EU’s external policies and initiatives, including through electoral observation missions. WE PROPOSE: The EEAS is launching a call for expression of interest for the recruitment of one SECRETARY (AST/SC2) as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of other servants of the EU in accordance with EEAS Decision Admin(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents. Please note that, candidates who have been engaged by the EEAS as non-permanent servants (temporary and contract agents engaged under Article 3b of the CEOS), will be bound by Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 14/07/2023 on the maximum duration of engagement by the European External Action Service of non-permanent staff under successive limited duration contracts of different types, and on the minimum lapse of time between successive contracts under Article 2(e) of the CEOS and repealing the Decision ADMIN(2020) 10 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 16/07/2020. WE LOOK FOR: A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: Carry out administrative duties for the Deputy Political Director/Managing Director’s office; Monitor annual representation budget, handle prior agreement forms and verify reimbursement in Ares. Compile annual planning from Divisions’ input; Monitor directorate’s annual mission budget. Request planning from Divisions. Process mission orders in MIPS+ for directorate staff and Head of Delegation; Coordination of Parliamentary Questions received for the Multilateral directorate; Document Management Coordinator (DMC) – help to ensure correct procedures regarding document handling/archiving; update filing plan as needed; Manage time management requests, under the authority of the Deputy Political Director/Managing Director/Deputy Managing Director, in Sysper; Interaction with HIVE team (Document Management and Information Division SCS.1), regarding use of collaborative tool and creation of Communities of Interest. LEGAL BASIS The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents The successful candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) at the grade of AST/SC2. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Candidates must meet ALL of the following general and specific conditions on the closing date for online applications : Be a national of one of the EU Member States and enjoy full rights as a citizen; Meet any obligations imposed on him or her by the laws concerning military service; Provide the appropriate character references as to their suitability for the performance of their duties; Have the capacity to work in languages of the CFSP in writing and orally. Secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, followed by at least 3 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties; OR Relevant professional training followed by at least 3 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents. In the case of applications from EU officials on leave for personal grounds, successful candidates will be reinstated into active employment within the meaning of Article 35(a) of the SR. SELECTION CRITERIA: Candidates should: Be well organised with the ability to deal with files in a timely manner; sound computer skills (MS Office) and good knowledge of standard internal procedures; Be familiar with IT applications (ARES, MIPS/MIPS+, Sysper, Decide, e-Brief, Rescom) and administrative procedures; Have experience of VTC applications such as WEBEX, Skype for Business, Teams, etc.; Be able to perform multiple tasks and adjust to changing priorities and respect deadlines; Have a very good knowledge of oral and written English and French; Previous experience in an EU-Institution. Furthermore: would be considered as strong assets EXPRESSION OF INTEREST AND SELECTION PROCEDURE: The selection procedure will take place in three different and successive steps: 1. Expression of Interest Before submitting their application, candidates should carefully check whether they meet all the eligibility criteria in order to avoid exclusion from the selection procedure. Expressions of interest should be sent by e-mail to the following functional mailbox POL-MULTILATERAL-MD@eeas.europa.eu copying AST-SC-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu For the purposes of the e-mail application, the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: " EoI-HQ-TA2b-AST/SC2-POL.MULTILATERAL- job 516927" Such an expression of interest must be accompanied by: The deadline for submission of expressions is 21/08/2026 at 12:00 midday (Brussels time). For correspondence concerning the selection procedure, please use the following email address (the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: " EoI-HQ-TA2b-AST/SC2-POL.MULTILATERAL- job 516927" ) : AST-SC-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu 2. Pre-selection The selection panel will make a pre-selection on the basis of the qualifications and the professional experience described in the CV and motivation letter. 3. Selection The candidates who have passed the pre-selection step will be invited for an interview so that the selection panel can evaluate them objectively and impartially based on the selection criteria, as listed in the present call for expression of interest. Additional specific written or oral tests might be organised by the panel. Following a comparative assessment of the merits of the preselected candidates, the selection panel will recommend the name of a candidate to the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment, and possibly, name(s) of other candidate(s) that should be placed on a reserve list valid for maximum 12 months. That list would be used, on the one hand, in case of refusal of the offer or unavailability of the recommended candidate in the present procedure and/or, on the other hand, for other future similar recruitment needs. Depending on the outcome of future appointment procedure(s) under Article 29 of the SR for a similar profile , EEAS services may, in case no suitable candidates are found among EU officials, have other job opportunities that would involve the recruitment of the Temporary Agents under Article 2(b) of the CEOS. If any, candidates in the above-mentioned reserve list may be contacted by other EEAS services for potential recruitment. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion . The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States. item.title: Vacancy notice – Policy Officer - Human Security issues/Sanctions Regime - Global GI.4 - Contract Agent FGIV - EEAS Headquarters – Job No 285568
item.description: The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. EEAS Global GI.4 "Migration and Human Security" deals with the external aspects of the EU's migration policy and human security, which comprises aspects of the fight against organised crime - drug trafficking, migrant smuggling and trafficking in human beings, including the multilateral aspects of those works strands. Our role is to contribute to the strategic planning and coordination of the EEAS work on these matters as well as to enhance internal/external policy consistency, develop synergies and integrate the above issues into the EU's overall relations with third countries and partners. We are also involved in the programming of the EU Global Fund budget in this field. We work in close cooperation with other EEAS departments, Member States, the European Commission and the Council Secretariat, and the relevant UN Agencies. We work in close cooperation with other EEAS departments, Member States, the European Commission and the Council Secretariat. The GI.4 Division has a highly motivated team with each member working flexibly with all colleagues, including from other divisions across the EEAS. Many of the issues dealt with are politically highly visible and connect with the headline goals of the HRVP and our senior management. WE PROPOSE The position of Policy Officer contract agent FGIV as per Article 3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). The successful candidate will have a pivotal role within a small, dynamic, enthusiastic team of friendly colleagues. The position offers the opportunity to contribute to advancing the EU agenda worldwide, including through interacting with the network of EU Delegations, EEAS geographical divisions, Commission services, EU agencies and Member States. The successful candidate will help drive policy in the field of human security, including by contributing, as appropriate, to the ongoing negotiations in the Council on the draft proposal for the new EU sanctions regime to counter threats from migrant smuggling, human trafficking and other forms of organised crime, and once adopted to contribute to its implementation. The successful candidate will also liaise with the EEAS Multilateral Division and the EUDEL Vienna, to contribute to work in the area of organised crime, and as appropriate contribute to the work of Council Working Parties, inter alia, in the area of judicial cooperation. Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function group IV), as per Article 3b of the CEOS, on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of one year. This contract may be successively renewed up to a maximum duration of six years, subject to the maximum duration of engagement by the EEAS allowed under successive limited duration contracts of different types. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT ‎EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available: 1 September 2026 LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof. WE LOOK FOR Under the authority of the Head of Division of Global Issues GI 4, the candidate is expected to perform the following tasks: Contribute to the implementation of EU policy in the human security portfolio of the division, including the new EU sanctions regime, in cooperation with relevant EEAS and Commission services as well as other relevant stakeholders. Contribute to the development of close cooperation, and carry out outreach actions, on the human security portfolio with partner countries, in coordination with other EEAS and Commission services concerned and EU Delegations. Contribute to identifying and addressing gaps in the human security portfolio, and support bilateral, regional and multilateral strategies in cooperation with the Commission, EEAS geographical divisions and with relevant third countries. Contribute to multilateral aspects, in close cooperation with the EU delegation in Vienna and the UNODC. Prepare briefings, analytical and background documents on the human security portfolio, and as relevant, contribute to strategy papers and briefings, in coordination with other EEAS and Commission services concerned and EU Delegations. Represent the EEAS in relevant fora, including with EU Member States, to present related work and facilitate the implementation of relevant strategies. Ensure interface with international organisations, civil society and academia, and attend conferences, seminars, committees, external meetings etc. As appropriate, the successful candidate may also be requested to support the work of the Division on other areas related to human security, as appropriate, and to support the work of other Council Working Parties, inter alia in the area of justice cooperation. Eligibility criteria In addition to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS and in the Commission Decision C(2017) 6760 final , which is applicable to the EEAS by virtue of the Decision ADMIN(2018) 4 of the High Representative, candidates must: have passed a valid EPSO CAST in FG IV, or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST for FG IV ( https://eu-careers.europa.eu/en/contract-staff-selection-procedures-always-open-registration ). In the latter case, while the registration will make the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the CAST exam; have completed university studies of at least three years attested by a diploma; have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties; be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen. Selection criteria Candidates should have: at least three years of experience in policy areas relevant to the position (e.g. sanctions, fight against migrant smuggling and trafficking of human beings, and / or other forms of organised crime); the ability to maintain diplomatic relations and to ensure representation and communication in a complex, multicultural environment; the capacity to create constructive working relations with national authorities, civil society, international organisations and EU Member States; strong drafting and analytical skills combined with sound judgement; knowledge of external relations, internal policies and functioning of the Union; excellent communication skills and the ability to establish and maintain a network of contacts both within and outside the EEAS; the ability to communicate clearly on complex issues and the capacity to perform with accuracy and in a flexible manner a diversity of tasks in a complex institutional environment; strong service attitude; be a flexible team player. Furthermore: capacity to work in Spanish experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; experience in working with or within other EU institutions; and/or international organisations, such as the United Nations, or similar institutional environments relevant working experience in the areas of human security and/or sanctions regimes; experience of international negotiations; experience in communication on the relevant policy areas; will be considered as strong assets. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality, of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks. In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest. MEDICAL CLEARANCE The signature of the contract will be subject to prior favourable opinion of the Medical Service, unless the successful candidate is a temporary agent currently employed in the EEAS. PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE (hereafter, “PSC”) The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC”) iss

item.title: Call for Expression of Interest 2026-EoI-HQ (AD) for the recruitment of one Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) Policy Officer in the Information and Document Management Division (RM.SCS.1)
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the networkof 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/ organisation. Within the EEAS, the Division "Information and Document Management" works to foster information management practices across the EEAS. Information is the raw material behind every one of our activities. Increasing our proficiency with information management will positively boost the overall performance of the whole institution. The Division carries out these tasks by working on the domains of information, records and archives management with the support of three dedicated teams. Furthermore, we are coordinating the meetings of the Information Management Committee (IMC) to support the implementation of the EEAS Information Management Strategy. WE PROPOSE The position of a Policy Officer in the Division for Information and Document Management. This position is classified as an “Administrator” type of post 1 in the grade AD 7. As temporary agents under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (hereafter, the “CEOS”), the duration of the assignment to the post shall, in principle, be four years dependent on the maximum duration of engagement in the EEAS allowed by their type of contract 2. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT EEAS Headquarters, Brussels,Belgium Post available: immediately LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The successful candidate for this position will be appointed in accordance with Article 29(1)(a) and Article 98(1), second subparagraph, of the Staff Regulations (SR) and Article 2(b) of the CEOS. WE LOOK FOR Under the authority of the Head of Division, the successful candidate will: contribute to the implementation of the EEAS’ Information Management Strategy and the EEAS Records Management and Archives Policy (ERMA); contribute to the development of policies, procedures and related documents; carry out related monitoring and reporting; and represent the EEAS in related groups and fora. Eligibility criteria 3 : In addition to the conditions set out in Article 12 of the CEOS, candidates must: Have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations (English and French); possess a level of education: which corresponds to completed university studies attested by a diploma when the normal period of university education is four years or more, OR which corresponds to completed university studies attested by a diploma and relevant professional experience of at least one year when the normal period of university education is at least three years. have at least 6 years full-time professional experience. This experience must have been gained after obtaining the four-year diploma or after obtaining the three-year diploma and the one-year relevant professional experience. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents and are ineligible. Selection criteria: Candidates should have: an excellent ability to maintain diplomatic relations and to ensure representation, communication in a complex, multicultural environment; an excellent capacity to create constructive working relations with national authorities, civil society, international organizations and EU Member States; strong drafting, communication and analytical skills combined with sound judgement; excellent knowledge of the EU's internal and external policies and instruments, and of the functioning of the Union and its inter-institutional framework; excellent knowledge of information management policies and related standards. Furthermore experience with: policies and standards related to the implementation of Artificial Intelligence; drafting and implementation of administrative policies; monitoring and reporting in a horizontal service; would be considered assets. TYPE AND DURATION OF CONTRACT FOR NEW TEMPORARY AGENTS The successful candidate will be offered a contract of temporary agent under Article 2(b) of the CEOS. Such contracts may not exceed 4 years in duration and can be renewed only once for a 2-year period, in accordance with Article 8, second indent, of the CEOS. All newly engaged temporary staff will be required to complete a probationary period of 9 months, in accordance with Article 14 of the CEOS. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks. In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest ( Annex I ). MEDICAL CLEARANCE If the successful candidate is not a temporary agent currently employed in the EEAS, he/she will be required to undergo a medical examination to ensure that he/she is physically fit to perform the duties. PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS 4 . The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC” 5 ) issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned. Candidates who do not already have a valid PSC will be required to go through the security clearance vetting procedure of their Member State to obtain this clearance in accordance with national laws and regulations and with the procedure laid down in the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 and in Annex A I of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . Until the PSC is issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned, the selected candidate will not be authorised to access EUCI at the level of CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL or above, or to participate in any meetings or workflow where EUCI is processed. Please note that the necessary procedure for obtaining a PSC can be initiated on request of the employer only, and not by the individual candidate. In case of failure to obtain or renew the required PSC, the AACC may take the appropriate measures in accordance with Article 7 of the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organization where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion. The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States. The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR. If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an email to EEAS-HQ-APPLICATIONS-AD@eeas.europa.eu . Your request will be treated in strict confidence and no record will be kept. If a candidate with a disability is selected for a vacant post, the EEAS is committed to providing reasonable accommodation in accordance with Article 1(d)(4) of the SR. All selected candidates are expected to adhere to the Principles of Professional Behaviour of the EEAS, which outline the need for integrity, transparency, respect, professionalism and accountability, and a zero tolerance approach to any form of harassment.
